summary_html: A **court reverses or vacates** a CPS or agency decision due to procedural error, insufficient evidence, or constitutional violation. Federal review data (CFSR, ASFA) tracks judicial determinations on reasonable efforts and due process.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — judicial findings of 'reasonable efforts' compliance  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of judicial/agency conformity  
- **42 U.S.C. § 1983** — civil-rights remedy for unconstitutional removals (14th & 4th Amendments).

key_cases.holding: The court held that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes an appeal from any final order in a dependency or neglect proceeding, that subsection (2) adds to rather than limits that right, and that C.A.R. 3.4(a) cannot narrow the categories of orders the statute makes appealable.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Colorado Supreme Court's statement of the appellate jurisdiction through which agency and trial-court errors in dependency cases are corrected.
key_cases.quote: we hold that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes the appeal of any order from a dependency or neglect proceeding that is "final"

key_cases.case_name: Wilson v. State Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The division reversed, holding that the central registry director could not amend a confirmed child-abuse report without good cause and prior notice to the subject, that the amended reports had to be expunged, and that findings resting on an uncharged incident violated the subject's procedural due process rights.
key_cases.relevance: The court reversed the agency's refusal to expunge and ordered relief, an example of judicial correction of an agency finding made without required notice.
key_cases.quote: the statute requires that notice of a proposed amendment be given so that the subject of the report may dispute the existence of "good cause" for that amendment.

key_cases.holding: The division held that section 19-1-126(1)(a) required the department to make new ICWA inquiries in this case, and that findings and orders from a sibling's earlier case could not alone support a determination that ICWA did not apply; the judgment was reversed and the case remanded.
key_cases.relevance: The court reversed a termination judgment outright for the department's and trial court's failure to conduct the statutory ICWA inquiry.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the findings and orders from the prior case alone are insufficient to support the trial court's conclusion that ICWA does not apply in this case.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the court of appeals and upheld the termination order, holding that the division failed to apply the clearly erroneous standard and improperly substituted its own view of witness credibility and of the weight, sufficiency and probative value of the evidence for the trial court's.
key_cases.relevance: It marks the outer limit of judicial correction of a termination: a reviewing court may not reverse by reweighing credibility and evidence that the record in fact supports.
key_cases.quote: we set aside a trial court's factual findings only when they are "so clearly erroneous as to find no support in the record."
